title: Epothilone B and isoflurane in rats
description: The 2024 eNeuro study reports that male rats receiving the microtubule-stabilizing drug epothilone B took an average of 69 seconds longer to reach loss of righting reflex during 4% isoflurane exposure.
limitations: The experiment used eight male rats, a behavioral proxy for anesthetic-induced unconsciousness, one anesthetic, and one drug. It did not directly measure quantum coherence or conscious experience.

title: Loss of righting reflex is a limited proxy
description: An anesthesia review explains that loss of righting reflex is a practical animal proxy but cannot, on its own, establish consciousness or the content of experience.
limitations: These reviews assess the measure in general; they do not negate the reported behavioral effect in the eNeuro experiment.

title: Quantum-consciousness proposals remain unconfirmed
description: Recent critical reviews describe microtubule quantum-processing claims as contested and note that the needed stability, reproducibility, and in-vivo evidence have not been independently established.
limitations: A review maps outstanding problems; it is not a direct replication of the 2024 rat experiment.

title: Popular Mechanics' interpretation
description: The article accurately identifies the rat study as its central source, then extends its implications to quantum consciousness and universe-wide entanglement.
limitations: This is science journalism, not independent experimental evidence; its broader interpretation is not tested by the rat experiment.
